references.text: Moses gives detailed instructions about the tithe every third year, which is to be given to the Levites, foreigners, fatherless children, and widows—an expansion of the command in Deut. 14:28.
The basis for the law of tithing is found here, where all tithes from the land belong to the Lord and are holy to him.
The tithe is given to the Levites as their inheritance for their service in the tabernacle, which is the background for the distribution mentioned in Deuteronomy 14:28.
Amos criticizes Israel's superficial practice of tithing, showing how the commandment on tithing from Deuteronomy was practiced and misused.
Malachi urges the people to bring the full tithe into the storehouse, referring back to the laws of tithing in Deuteronomy.
Earlier in the same book, instructions are given about where the tithe is to be eaten and a reminder not to forget the Levite.
